entries.meaning: An edit preserves the relation between a quantity, its entity, measurement unit and condition, not merely the presence of each token.
entries.guidance: Check source-to-draft omissions and draft-to-source additions within the requested unit.
entries.avoid: Keeping two scores but swapping the methods, denominator, metric direction or evaluation setting.
conditions: Apply to factual rewriting, translation and result reporting.
exceptions: An abstract may omit secondary detail when its remaining claim stays accurate; necessary scope cannot be omitted.
evidence_required: Located author facts and their original relationships.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: A succeeds in 8 of 10 trials; B in 6 of 10 trials.
examples: A succeeds in 8 of 10 trials, compared with 6 of 10 for B.

counter_examples.text: B succeeds in 8 of 10 trials, outperforming A.
counter_examples.why: The entity-score assignment and comparison direction are reversed.

entries.expression: Separate exemplar style from manuscript evidence
entries.meaning: A reference can teach an explanatory choice without establishing our method's result or novelty.
entries.guidance: Transfer the reader-facing function only when the author's materials support it; establish citation support independently.
entries.avoid: Copying a source paper's mechanism, speedup or claim strength into our paper.
conditions: Use whenever drafting from an exemplar or sentence scaffold.
exceptions: The same publication may also support a cited claim, but that support must be checked separately.
evidence_required: Exemplar location and a separate author evidence anchor.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: the exemplar has a proven equivalence; our project has only runtime measurements.
examples: We describe the proposed simplification and report its measured runtime.

counter_examples.text: Our simplification is mathematically equivalent to the original objective.
counter_examples.why: The source's proof cannot establish equivalence for this project.

entries.expression: Attach consequential scope to the claim
entries.meaning: Conditions that change a result's interpretation remain recoverable where the result is claimed.
entries.guidance: Name the relevant population, budget, split or assumptions rather than appending an unrelated blanket disclaimer.
entries.avoid: Converting a result on a tested shift into general robustness or a conditional theorem into a universal guarantee.
conditions: Use when changing the condition could change the conclusion.
exceptions: A nearby unambiguous definition may supply the condition; do not repeat it mechanically in every sentence.
evidence_required: The evaluation population or theorem assumptions.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: a robot succeeds on held-out objects in a fixed task; new tasks were not tested.
examples: The policy transfers to held-out objects in the evaluated task.

counter_examples.text: The policy generalizes to unseen tasks.
counter_examples.why: The held-out axis changes from objects to tasks.

entries.meaning: A reader should understand what a design does, not merely recognize its component names.
entries.guidance: Explain a supported input-operation-output relation when a component list leaves the method unintelligible.
entries.avoid: Naming a scheduler, decoder and cache, then asserting that the system is effective.
conditions: Use when the reader cannot recover the relevant interaction from the surrounding text.
exceptions: An informative definition or formal result may carry the contribution without a mechanistic explanation.
evidence_required: Actual operations and dependencies; causal attribution needs separate evidence.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: a scheduler requests a new observation when the previous observation exceeds an age threshold.
examples: The scheduler requests a new observation once the current observation exceeds the age threshold.

counter_examples.text: Our age-aware scheduler improves observation quality and guarantees reliable control.
counter_examples.why: A name and intended role do not establish quality or a control guarantee.

source_notes.location: SKILL.md operating rules 3-4, 10-11 and rewrite method 3-4; references/essential-rules.md terms, noun groups and surface ambiguity
source_notes.observation: The skill prioritizes intended meaning, stable terminology and referent clarity. We extend the existing definition owner rather than adding a duplicate rule; academic voice and compound exceptions are local adaptations.

entries.expression: Define objects and symbols before using their relationships
entries.meaning: Definitions make the subject, operation and mathematical dependence recoverable.
entries.guidance: Introduce the relevant object and symbol, then explain the relation it participates in. Resolve ambiguous antecedents and modifier attachments using the author's defined relationships, not a guessed actor or forced synonym.
entries.avoid: Acronym chains, ambiguous pronouns and equations whose quantities are never identified.
conditions: Use for new symbols, resources, modules or ambiguous technical nouns.
Use when a pronoun or compact compound leaves two materially different technical readings.
exceptions: Standard notation may need only a compact definition; established definitions need not be repeated.
Keep unambiguous pronouns and standard compound terms; passive voice can retain the intended information focus when the known actor is not the topic.
evidence_required: Author definitions and the actual equation or implementation.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: tau is the age threshold used by the scheduler. A separate synthetic case: a teacher supplies pseudo-labels to a student, and only the student parameters change.
examples: Let tau denote the maximum observation age; the scheduler refreshes observations older than tau.
The teacher supplies pseudo-labels to the student; only the student is updated.

counter_examples.text: It uses tau to improve the system.
counter_examples.why: Neither the referent nor tau's operational meaning is recoverable.

counter_examples.text: The teacher supplies pseudo-labels to the student, and it is updated.
counter_examples.why: The ambiguous antecedent can assign the update to the teacher or the student; the author supplies the intended target.

source_notes.location: Abstract; evaluation conditions and model selection
source_notes.observation: Terminology context only; the conditional guidance and synthetic examples are local editorial synthesis.

entries.meaning: A result comparison answers a contribution question instead of merely restating table rows.
entries.guidance: Identify the informative contrast and retain resource or training differences that affect interpretation.
entries.avoid: Calling an unmatched-resource comparison a controlled component ablation.
conditions: Use when choosing and interpreting the main comparison.
exceptions: Unmatched stronger references may be useful if their distinct comparison role and resources remain explicit.
evidence_required: Comparator identity, controlled factors and relevant unmatched budgets.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: A uses additional demonstrations; B does not.
examples: A scores higher than B with an additional demonstration budget; this comparison does not isolate the architecture change.

counter_examples.text: The ablation proves that the architecture change causes the improvement.
counter_examples.why: Training data differs, so the named factor is not isolated.

source_notes.location: Abstract; aggregate scores, finite runs and uncertainty
source_notes.observation: Terminology context only; the conditional guidance and synthetic examples are local editorial synthesis.

entries.expression: Report the measurement unit and aggregation level
entries.meaning: Tasks, episodes, executions, seeds and sampled trajectories are different reporting units.
entries.guidance: Associate each count and average with its actual experimental scope; ask rather than infer a missing denominator.
entries.avoid: Turning sampled trajectories or repeated executions into independent training seeds.
conditions: Use for sample counts, rates and aggregate metrics.
exceptions: A declared table caption may supply a shared denominator; its scope must cover the particular comparison.
evidence_required: Numerator, denominator, aggregation rule and sampling unit.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: three trained policies each execute ten robot trials.
examples: We evaluate three trained policies with ten executions per policy.

counter_examples.text: We evaluate 30 independent training seeds.
counter_examples.why: Robot executions do not become independent model training runs.

source_notes.location: Abstract; aggregate scores, finite runs and uncertainty
source_notes.observation: Terminology context only; the conditional guidance and synthetic examples are local editorial synthesis.

entries.expression: Keep consequential uncertainty and its definition
entries.meaning: Dispersion and interval estimates qualify a result; different uncertainty summaries are not interchangeable.
entries.guidance: Retain supplied uncertainty where it changes interpretation and state whether it is SD, SE, CI or another declared summary.
entries.avoid: Inventing error bars or treating overlap as a significance test.
conditions: Use for close comparisons or claims depending on variability.
exceptions: Do not manufacture intervals for an unreplicated result; identify the reporting gap or narrow the claim.
evidence_required: Uncertainty definition, replication unit and interval or dispersion procedure.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: the author reports 0.72 plus/minus 0.03 as SD across seeds.
examples: The mean score is 0.72, with SD 0.03 across training seeds.

counter_examples.text: The 95% confidence interval is 0.72 plus/minus 0.03.
counter_examples.why: A reported SD cannot be relabeled as a confidence interval.

entries.meaning: Compression should not silently erase a supported contribution the author prioritizes.
entries.guidance: Allocate space according to supported promises, not a fixed five-sentence outline or metric quota.
entries.avoid: Keeping only empirical scores in a theory-plus-empirical abstract.
conditions: Use when compressing multiple confirmed contributions.
exceptions: Author-approved scope reductions can omit secondary contributions; no universal contribution-evidence ordering is imposed.
evidence_required: Confirmed priorities and evidence for each retained promise.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: the confirmed contribution includes a conditional bound and a measured runtime reduction.
examples: We establish the bound under assumption A and report lower runtime in the tested setting.

counter_examples.text: We introduce a faster implementation.
counter_examples.why: The author's prioritized theoretical contribution disappears.

entries.expression: Keep a stable term for a stable defined object
entries.meaning: Synonym variation can falsely suggest that one object is several different objects.
entries.guidance: Use the manuscript's operational definition; preserve distinct terms when they denote distinct quantities.
entries.avoid: Alternating episode, trajectory and demonstration as stylistic synonyms.
conditions: Use where referents or technical meanings could become ambiguous.
exceptions: Accepted abbreviations and explicitly defined equivalent names are fine; the dictionary is not an exhaustive whitelist.
evidence_required: Definitions and referent identity in this manuscript.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: the paper defines a demonstration as an expert-provided episode.
examples: We collect 20 demonstrations, each consisting of one expert-provided episode.

counter_examples.text: We collect 20 demonstrations and evaluate the 20 training seeds.
counter_examples.why: The second noun changes the unit instead of restating it.

entries.expression: Remove empty framing, not scientific qualifications
entries.meaning: Directness removes redundant framing without strengthening the scientific statement.
entries.guidance: Prefer an explicit subject and action where helpful; retain assumptions, negation, technical names and warranted uncertainty.
entries.avoid: Global bans on passive voice, -ing terms, long sentences or the word limitation.
conditions: Use when editing vague preambles or unnecessarily stacked clauses.
exceptions: Passive voice may appropriately foreground an experimental object; reinforcement learning is a protected technical term.
evidence_required: The original statement's scope and the sentence's actual rhetorical function.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: a proof holds only for bounded rewards.
examples: For bounded rewards, the estimator satisfies the stated bound.

counter_examples.text: The estimator always satisfies the bound.
counter_examples.why: Simplification removes the condition that licenses the claim.

entries.expression: Read the claim from prose before checking the plan
entries.meaning: A complete matrix does not establish that the actual prose communicates its intended relationship.
entries.guidance: Reconstruct the operation or comparison from the draft alone, then check the strongest reasonable reading against evidence.
entries.avoid: Supplying a missing relation from the writer's notes and marking the prose complete.
conditions: Use for a claim-bearing unit after drafting or compression.
exceptions: This is semantic self-review, not an independent source audit or evidence of better writing.
evidence_required: Final prose location, recoverable relationship and its evidence anchor.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: a draft names a routing module but never explains which observation it selects.
examples: The router selects the most recent observation that satisfies the visibility constraint.

counter_examples.text: Our visibility-aware router yields effective perception.
counter_examples.why: The intended selection operation remains only in working notes.

entries.meaning: Measure or assess under a specified protocol; the verb alone does not assert a favorable result.
entries.guidance: Use for a completed assessment and report its setting; distinguish planned evaluation.
entries.avoid: Replacing evaluate with demonstrate when the source reports only what was tested.
conditions: A protocol was actually executed.
exceptions: An introduction may describe planned evaluation explicitly in future tense.
evidence_required: Executed protocol or an explicit planned-work label.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: tests were run on four tasks, with mixed outcomes.
examples: We evaluate the policy on four tasks.

counter_examples.text: We demonstrate reliable performance on four tasks.
counter_examples.why: Completed testing does not establish reliability.

entries.meaning: Show a specific property or finding supported by the stated evidence, not every capability suggested by a design.
entries.guidance: Name the demonstrated outcome and its scope; preserve the source's evidential strength when reconstructing a paper.
entries.avoid: Using the verb to promote design intent, a small pilot or correlation into a broad validated mechanism.
conditions: The evidence directly supports the named outcome.
exceptions: Use propose, evaluate or observe if support is incomplete; demonstrate is not universally banned.
evidence_required: A located experiment, example or derivation supporting this particular outcome.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: a constructed example exhibits a failure of one estimator.
examples: The constructed example demonstrates a failure of the estimator under this shift.

counter_examples.text: The example demonstrates that all estimators fail under distribution shift.
counter_examples.why: The evidence covers one estimator and one constructed setting.

entries.meaning: Establish the stated formal proposition through a proof under explicit assumptions.
entries.guidance: Keep quantifiers, assumptions and the proved object; empirical support is not a mathematical proof.
entries.avoid: Claiming an ablation proves necessity or all-distribution robustness.
conditions: A proof of the actual proposition is available.
exceptions: Informal evidence may support a conjecture but should be described as evidence, not silently relabeled proof.
evidence_required: Proposition, assumptions and corresponding proof.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: a proof establishes a bound for bounded rewards.
examples: We prove the bound for bounded rewards.

counter_examples.text: Three successful runs prove the bound for all rewards.
counter_examples.why: Runs neither establish a theorem nor remove its assumptions.

source_notes.location: Abstract; aggregate scores, finite runs and uncertainty
source_notes.observation: Terminology context only; the conditional guidance and synthetic examples are local editorial synthesis.

entries.meaning: Statistical significance concerns a specified inferential procedure; practical importance is a separate judgment.
entries.guidance: Name the test or inferential criterion and the comparison. Otherwise report the measured difference without statistical implication.
entries.avoid: Treating a large percentage, overlapping error bars or a favorable average as a significance test.
conditions: Use statistically significant only when the stated procedure supports that inference.
exceptions: Non-statistical significant may mean important in ordinary prose, but avoid ambiguous metric claims; substantial also needs a justified interpretation.
evidence_required: Test or interval procedure, sampling unit, criterion and comparison; multiplicity handling when relevant.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: A scores 0.72 and B 0.69; no inferential procedure was supplied.
examples: A scores 0.72, compared with 0.69 for B.

counter_examples.text: A significantly outperforms B.
counter_examples.why: A difference in point estimates alone does not establish statistical significance.

entries.meaning: A declared property under specified perturbations, failures or assumptions; the mathematical sense may differ from an empirical claim.
entries.guidance: Name the robustness axis and evidence or the formal robustness definition.
entries.avoid: Using robust as praise for an unperturbed average score.
conditions: The paper defines and evaluates or proves the relevant robustness property.
exceptions: Keep robust inside an established algorithm name, but do not infer that the name validates a property.
evidence_required: Perturbation range and protocol, or a formal definition and proof.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: results cover three specified lighting perturbations only.
examples: Performance is retained under the three tested lighting perturbations.

counter_examples.text: The policy is robust to real-world variation.
counter_examples.why: The claim extends beyond the tested perturbation family.

entries.meaning: A benefit on a named resource axis, workload and comparison, not a synonym for small or fast in every setting.
entries.guidance: Specify memory, training compute, latency, throughput or interactions, retaining the quality and measurement boundary.
entries.avoid: Inferring lower wall-clock latency from fewer parameters or FLOPs alone.
conditions: The claimed resource benefit has a measurement or a properly scoped analytical bound.
exceptions: A parameter-efficient method name can be retained without claiming measured end-to-end speed.
evidence_required: Resource metric, hardware or analytical model, workload, comparator and quality scope.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: A has fewer parameters, but runtime has not been measured.
examples: A uses fewer parameters than B; runtime is not measured.

counter_examples.text: A runs faster because it has fewer parameters.
counter_examples.why: Parameter count does not determine measured latency.

source_notes.observation: Terminology context only; the conditional guidance and synthetic examples are local editorial synthesis.

entries.meaning: An explicitly specified target-task use without the target-task examples or adaptation excluded by that protocol; it does not imply no pretraining exposure.
entries.guidance: State zero with respect to what: labeled target examples, demonstrations, parameter updates or another declared budget.
entries.avoid: Calling a model universally unseen or adaptation-free merely because no target labels were used.
conditions: The protocol states which task information and adaptation are absent.
exceptions: Zero-shot classification, deployment and in-context prompting have different conventions; the manuscript's operational definition governs.
evidence_required: Target information budget, adaptation procedure and known pretraining exposure limits.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: a pretrained classifier uses text labels but no dataset-specific parameter fitting.
examples: We evaluate zero-shot classification without dataset-specific parameter fitting.

counter_examples.text: The model has never seen any related concept during training.
counter_examples.why: A zero-shot evaluation protocol does not establish pretraining absence.

entries.meaning: A stated small example budget under a named adaptation or conditioning procedure.
entries.guidance: Specify number, unit, selection and whether examples condition a prompt or train parameters.
entries.avoid: Treating four prompt examples and four robot demonstration episodes as the same training budget.
conditions: The example unit and adaptation procedure are specified.
exceptions: Different fields use different shot units; retain the established task convention and define it locally.
evidence_required: Example count and type, selection protocol and update mechanism.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: four labeled examples are supplied in context with fixed model parameters.
examples: We use four labeled in-context examples without parameter updates.

counter_examples.text: We fine-tune the model on four examples.
counter_examples.why: Prompt conditioning is not a parameter update.

source_notes.observation: Terminology context only; the conditional guidance and synthetic examples are local editorial synthesis.

entries.meaning: Additional training of a pretrained model or attached trainable parameters for a specified task or domain.
entries.guidance: State which parameters change, the data budget and training procedure; distinguish full and parameter-efficient updates.
entries.avoid: Equating retrieval or prompting alone with fine-tuning.
conditions: At least the declared model or adapter parameters undergo training updates.
exceptions: Adapter-only or LoRA training is fine-tuning even when base weights remain frozen.
evidence_required: Trainable parameters, data, objective and update procedure.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: only low-rank adapters are trained; base weights are frozen.
examples: We fine-tune low-rank adapters while keeping the base weights frozen.

counter_examples.text: No fine-tuning occurs because the base weights remain frozen.
counter_examples.why: Trainable adapter updates are omitted from the statement.

source_notes.observation: Terminology context only; the conditional guidance and synthetic examples are local editorial synthesis.
Terminology context only; the conditional guidance and synthetic examples are local editorial synthesis.

entries.meaning: The declared training stage preceding the focal adaptation or downstream evaluation.
entries.guidance: Name the pretrained checkpoint, known data scope and distinction from target adaptation; disclose unknown coverage.
entries.avoid: Claiming unseen evaluation concepts solely because downstream training excludes them.
conditions: A prior trained checkpoint or prior training stage is used.
exceptions: A staged system may have several pretraining stages; define the reference stage rather than forcing a single global label.
evidence_required: Checkpoint provenance and available training-data disclosure.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: the base checkpoint's complete training corpus is unknown.
examples: We use the pretrained checkpoint; overlap with its undisclosed training corpus cannot be excluded.

counter_examples.text: All test concepts are unseen during pretraining.
counter_examples.why: An undisclosed corpus cannot support this exclusion.

source_notes.observation: Terminology context only; the conditional guidance and synthetic examples are local editorial synthesis.

entries.meaning: The declared procedure that produces predictions, samples or actions; it may include additional test-time computation.
entries.guidance: State the procedure and timing boundary, including search, sampling or adaptation when present.
entries.avoid: Treating a single forward-pass time as the cost of an entire decision pipeline.
conditions: The prediction or action-generation procedure is specified.
exceptions: Test-time adaptation can update parameters; do not assert inference always means fixed weights.
evidence_required: Execution steps and the measured or reported boundary.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: prediction includes one adaptation update before a forward pass.
examples: The inference procedure updates the adapter once before predicting.

counter_examples.text: Inference requires only a forward pass with fixed parameters.
counter_examples.why: The declared procedure includes an adapter update before prediction.

source_notes.observation: Terminology context only; the conditional guidance and synthetic examples are local editorial synthesis.

entries.meaning: A declared change to model parameters, statistics or state using information available at test time.
entries.guidance: Report target information, updated quantities, update budget and reset or persistence policy.
entries.avoid: Calling target-adapted predictions adaptation-free or hiding test-time updates from efficiency measurements.
conditions: The procedure adapts a declared quantity at test time.
exceptions: The specific adaptation mechanism differs across methods; extra search alone need not be described as parameter adaptation.
evidence_required: Update rule, data access, cost and state persistence.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: normalization statistics are updated using unlabeled target batches.
examples: We update normalization statistics on unlabeled target batches at test time.

counter_examples.text: The model uses no target information.
counter_examples.why: Unlabeled target batches are still target information.

source_notes.observation: Terminology context only; the conditional guidance and synthetic examples are local editorial synthesis.

entries.meaning: A specified shift relative to a declared reference distribution; held-out samples alone do not imply distribution shift.
entries.guidance: Name the reference, held-out axis and actual shift construction or observed population change.
entries.avoid: Calling an ordinary random test split OOD because its individual samples are unseen.
conditions: The declared evaluation differs on the specified distributional axis.
exceptions: Operational OOD definitions vary; report the chosen construction without claiming all distribution shifts.
evidence_required: Reference distribution, split design and shift axis.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: evaluation is a random split from the same sampled population.
examples: We evaluate on a held-out random split from the same population.

counter_examples.text: The random test split establishes OOD robustness.
counter_examples.why: Sample separation neither defines a shift nor establishes broad robustness.

source_notes.location: Abstract; evaluation conditions and model selection
source_notes.observation: Terminology context only; the conditional guidance and synthetic examples are local editorial synthesis.

entries.meaning: Performance beyond the fitting data on a specified sample, object, task or distribution axis, or a precisely stated formal generalization property.
entries.guidance: State what is held out, how selection is separated and whether the claim is empirical or formal.
entries.avoid: Converting held-out objects into unseen tasks or empirical transfer into a universal bound.
conditions: The claimed axis and the evaluation or proof supporting it are available.
exceptions: A theory result can concern generalization without an empirical shift experiment; retain its assumptions and quantifiers.
evidence_required: Held-out unit and selection protocol, or the exact theorem and proof.
entries.example_context: Synthetic: tests hold out objects but retain training task instructions.
examples: We assess generalization to held-out objects under the same task instructions.

counter_examples.text: The experiment proves generalization to new tasks.
counter_examples.why: Neither the held-out axis nor the evidential status matches.
